customer_question: Our product comes with an optional plastic cover (resin cover, not related to Bluetooth). Do we need to include this accessory in the Bluetooth SIG registration?
question_variants: Do non-Bluetooth accessories need to be registered with the SIG?
Does an optional plastic case/cover need to be included in Bluetooth certification?
Which optional accessories must be included in a Bluetooth SIG registration?
actual_issue: Customer IDEAL Co. asked whether a plastic/resin cover that ships as an optional accessory with their Bluetooth product needed to be included in the SIG registration. The cover has no Bluetooth function.
plain_english_explanation: Only items that contain or affect Bluetooth functionality need to be included in the SIG registration. Optional accessories that have no relationship to Bluetooth (such as a plastic cover, carrying case, or other passive accessories) do not need to be registered.
consultant_answer: Optional accessories like a plastic/resin cover that have no Bluetooth function do not need to be included in the SIG registration. Only the Bluetooth-enabled product itself (and any components that implement Bluetooth) are registered.
decision_logic: SIG registration scope = Bluetooth-capable products and components only. Non-Bluetooth accessories, packaging, and passive attachments are outside the registration scope. The SIG certification applies to the Bluetooth implementation, not the physical package it ships with.
final_recommendation: Exclude non-Bluetooth optional accessories from the registration scope. If any accessory contains Bluetooth hardware (e.g., a Bluetooth-enabled charging case), include it. Passive accessories with no Bluetooth function are always excluded.
risk_if_done_wrong: Incorrectly including non-Bluetooth accessories adds unnecessary products to the registration and may create confusion about what is being certified. Excluding a Bluetooth-capable accessory would mean it is used without valid certification.
